strings.hub.mass.title: The Holy Mass
strings.hub.mass.subtitle: The Church's central act of worship
strings.hub.mass.intro: The same sacrifice offered on Calvary, made present on the altar; the Word proclaimed and the Bread broken. Here is how the Mass is ordered, and the sacred things used within it.
strings.sec.structure.title: The Structure of the Mass
strings.sec.structure.summary: Four movements, from the gathering of the people to the sending out.
strings.stepper.structure.title: The Order of Mass
strings.stepper.structure.intro: The Mass unfolds in a clear order — two great tables, the Word and the Eucharist, framed by the rites that gather and send the assembly.
strings.stepper.structure.intro.title: Introductory Rites
strings.stepper.structure.intro.body: The gathering: the entrance procession, the sign of the cross and greeting, the Penitential Act, the Gloria, and the opening prayer that gathers the assembly before God.
strings.stepper.structure.word.title: Liturgy of the Word
strings.stepper.structure.word.body: God speaks: the readings from Scripture, the Responsorial Psalm, the Gospel, the homily, the Profession of Faith (Creed) and the Prayer of the Faithful.
strings.stepper.structure.eucharist.title: Liturgy of the Eucharist
strings.stepper.structure.eucharist.body: The heart of the Mass: the gifts of bread and wine are prepared and offered, the Eucharistic Prayer consecrates them into the Body and Blood of Christ, and the faithful receive Holy Communion.
strings.stepper.structure.concluding.title: Concluding Rites
strings.stepper.structure.concluding.body: The sending: a final blessing and the dismissal — “Go forth, the Mass is ended” — from the Latin of which (Ite, missa est) the very word “Mass” is drawn.
strings.sec.procession.title: The Entrance Procession
strings.sec.procession.summary: The ministers enter in an order that expresses reverence, unity, and the journey toward the altar.
strings.stepper.procession.title: Who Walks In, and Why
strings.stepper.procession.intro: The Entrance Procession is the opening rite of the Mass. The ministers enter the church in an order that expresses reverence, unity, and the journey toward the altar where Christ is present.
strings.stepper.procession.thurifer.title: Thurible Bearer
strings.stepper.procession.thurifer.body: The thurible bearer leads with burning incense, a sign of our prayers rising up to God.
strings.stepper.procession.cross.title: Cross Bearer
strings.stepper.procession.cross.body: The processional cross leads the ministers forward, the sign of Christ who goes before us.
strings.stepper.procession.candle.title: Candle Bearers
strings.stepper.procession.candle.body: Acolytes carry lit candles beside the cross — Christ, the Light of the World.
strings.stepper.procession.bell.title: Bell Ringer
strings.stepper.procession.bell.body: A bell is rung to announce the procession and to call the faithful to worship.
strings.stepper.procession.book.title: Book Bearer
strings.stepper.procession.book.body: The Book of the Gospels is carried aloft — the Word of God proclaimed in the Mass.
strings.stepper.procession.priest.title: The Priest
strings.stepper.procession.priest.body: The priest follows as the one who presides. He represents Christ himself, the Head of the Church.
strings.sec.mass.monstrance.title: The Monstrance
strings.sec.mass.monstrance.summary: Base, shaft, sunburst and luna — the parts of the vessel of Eucharistic adoration.
strings.art.monstrance.title: The Monstrance
strings.art.monstrance.lead: The vessel that displays the Blessed Sacrament for adoration.
strings.art.monstrance.p1: The monstrance — from the Latin monstrare, “to show” — is a sacred vessel that holds the consecrated Host up for the faithful to see and adore. It is used for Eucharistic Adoration, Benediction and processions.
strings.art.monstrance.callout.title: It is not worshipped
strings.art.monstrance.callout.body: The monstrance itself is not adored — it is a sacred vessel that points us to Jesus, truly present in the Eucharist.
strings.art.monstrance.li_cross: **Cross** — at the very top, the sign of our salvation in Christ.
strings.art.monstrance.li_sunburst: **Sunburst (rays of glory)** — the golden rays that represent the radiance of Christ, the “Sun of Justice.”
strings.art.monstrance.li_window: **Ostensorium (the window)** — the central round opening that displays the Eucharist for adoration.
strings.art.monstrance.li_luna: **Luna** — the crescent-shaped clip that holds the Host in place; its shape recalls the moon, a symbol of Our Lady.
strings.art.monstrance.li_host: **The Host** — the Blessed Sacrament itself: the Body, Blood, Soul and Divinity of Jesus Christ.
strings.art.monstrance.li_node: **Node** — the knop on the stem, often worked with wheat and vine — the Bread of Life and the True Vine.
strings.art.monstrance.li_shaft: **Shaft** — the stem that lifts the Host high, our journey in faith raised toward Christ.
strings.art.monstrance.li_base: **Base** — the broad foot that gives stability and honours the sacred presence it bears.
strings.sec.mass.thurible.title: The Thurible
strings.sec.mass.thurible.summary: Bowl, lid, chains and cross — the parts of the censer, and what its smoke means.
strings.art.thurible.title: The Thurible
strings.art.thurible.lead: The censer in which incense is burned, a sign of prayer rising to God.
strings.art.thurible.p1: The thurible is a sacred vessel used to burn incense. The rising smoke is a sign of our prayers ascending to God — “Let my prayer be counted as incense before you” (Psalm 141:2). It is used at the Entrance, the Gospel, the Preparation of the Gifts, the Eucharistic Prayer and Benediction.
strings.art.thurible.callout.title: Why the smoke
strings.art.thurible.callout.body: The incense stands for our prayers, the rising smoke for those prayers ascending to God, and the sweet fragrance honours God and sanctifies the space.
strings.art.thurible.li_finial: **Finial (cross)** — the cross on top, a reminder that our prayers are offered in the name of Christ.
strings.art.thurible.li_lid: **Lid (cover)** — the perforated cover that lets the smoke rise, symbolising prayers ascending to heaven.
strings.art.thurible.li_charcoal: **Charcoal plate** — holds the burning charcoal on which the incense is placed.
strings.art.thurible.li_bowl: **Censer bowl** — the cup that holds the charcoal and incense, the heart of the thurible.
strings.art.thurible.li_chains: **Chains** — usually three, for faith, hope and love; they balance the thurible as it is swung.
strings.art.thurible.li_ring: **Suspension ring** — the ring at the top from which the chains hang.
strings.art.thurible.li_handle: **Handle** — used by the thurifer to raise the lid and swing the thurible during the liturgy.
strings.sec.vessels.title: Sacred Vessels
strings.sec.vessels.summary: Chalice, paten, ciborium and the other vessels that serve at the altar.
strings.art.vessels.title: The Vessels of the Altar
strings.art.vessels.lead: The sacred vessels that hold and carry the Body and Blood of Christ.
strings.art.vessels.p1: Because they hold the Eucharist, the vessels of the altar are made of precious metal (or lined with it), blessed for sacred use, and handled only with reverence.
strings.art.vessels.li_chalice: **Chalice** — the cup that holds the wine which becomes the Blood of Christ.
strings.art.vessels.li_paten: **Paten** — the small plate that holds the priest's host.
strings.art.vessels.li_ciborium: **Ciborium** — the covered cup that holds the hosts for the Communion of the faithful and reserves them in the tabernacle.
strings.art.vessels.li_cruets: **Cruets** — the small jugs of wine and water brought to the altar at the Preparation of the Gifts.
strings.art.vessels.li_pyx: **Pyx** — the small round case used to carry Communion to the sick.
strings.art.vessels.li_luna: **Luna & monstrance** — the crescent clip and the rayed vessel that display the Host for adoration.
strings.art.vessels.callout.title: The linens
strings.art.vessels.callout.body: White cloths serve alongside the vessels: the corporal on which they stand, the purificator for wiping the chalice, and the pall that covers it.
strings.sec.postures.title: Postures & Responses
strings.sec.postures.summary: When to stand, sit and kneel — and the words the people make their own.
strings.art.postures.title: Praying with the Body
strings.art.postures.lead: At Mass the whole body prays. The common postures and responses bind the assembly into one voice.
strings.art.postures.p1: The faithful stand, sit and kneel together at set moments — a shared language of reverence that expresses one faith in one body.
strings.art.postures.li_stand: **Standing** — for prayer and to honour the Gospel; the posture of the risen and attentive.
strings.art.postures.li_sit: **Sitting** — for the readings before the Gospel and the homily, the posture of listening.
strings.art.postures.li_kneel: **Kneeling** — during the Eucharistic Prayer and before Communion, the posture of adoration and humility.
strings.art.postures.li_genuflect: **Genuflection** — bending the right knee toward the tabernacle, adoring Christ present in the Eucharist.
strings.art.postures.li_bow: **Bowing** — a bow of the head at the holy names, and a deeper bow before receiving Communion.
strings.art.postures.li_sign: **The Sign of the Cross** — made at the beginning and end, marking the whole prayer as Christ's.
strings.art.postures.p2: Throughout the Mass the people answer the priest. To “The Lord be with you” they reply “And with your spirit”; the readings close with “Thanks be to God” and “Praise to you, Lord Jesus Christ”; and to the great prayers the assembly seals its assent with “Amen.”
strings.sec.altar.title: The Altar
strings.sec.altar.summary: The table of sacrifice — how it is dressed, the cloths that cover it, and the crosses cut into its stone.
strings.art.altar.title: The Altar
strings.art.altar.lead: At once the table of the Lord's Supper and the altar of his sacrifice — the focus of the whole church.
strings.art.altar.p1: The altar is the heart of the church building. It is at once the table of the Lord's Supper, where the faithful are fed, and the altar of sacrifice, where the offering of Calvary is made present. Because of this the altar stands for Christ himself, and the priest reverences it with a bow and a kiss at the beginning and end of Mass.
strings.art.altar.p2: Nothing is placed on the altar but what the celebration requires. It is dressed simply and with dignity, its ornament following the liturgical colour of the season.
strings.art.altar.li_cross: **The cross** — a cross bearing the figure of the crucified Christ stands on or near the altar, kept in view of the assembly.
strings.art.altar.li_candles: **Candles** — at least two lit candles (up to six, or seven for a bishop) stand on or beside the altar, a sign of reverence and festivity.
strings.art.altar.li_cloth: **The altar cloth** — at least one white cloth covers the altar top, out of reverence for what is celebrated upon it.
strings.art.altar.li_flowers: **Flowers** — may adorn the altar in moderation according to the season; never during Lent, and only sparingly in Advent.
strings.art.altar.li_frontal: **The frontal** — an antependium may hang before the altar in the colour of the day.
strings.art.altar.p3: The linens used at the altar are white, blessed for sacred use, and handled with great care. Some cover the altar itself; others serve at the moment of Communion.
strings.art.altar.li_altarcloth: **The altar cloth (“fair linen”)** — the white cloth, traditionally of linen, that covers the altar table; in earlier custom three cloths were used together.
strings.art.altar.li_corporal: **The corporal** — a square white cloth unfolded at the centre of the altar, on which the chalice and paten rest so that no fragment of the Host is lost.
strings.art.altar.li_purificator: **The purificator** — a small folded cloth used to wipe the chalice and the priest's fingers.
strings.art.altar.li_pall: **The pall** — a stiff linen-covered square laid over the chalice to keep anything from falling into it.
strings.art.altar.p4: When a new altar is dedicated, the bishop anoints it with sacred chrism and incenses it. Five crosses are carved or marked into it — one at each corner and one in the centre — recalling the five wounds of Christ. In many altars the relics of a saint, often a martyr, are sealed within or beneath the altar stone, an ancient link to the tombs on which the early Church offered Mass.
strings.art.altar.callout.title: Why the kiss
strings.art.altar.callout.body: The priest kisses the altar because it stands for Christ, the cornerstone. At a solemn Mass it is also honoured with incense — the same reverence shown to the Gospel and to the gifts.
